source.title: Some Open Problems in Sasaki Geometry

accepted.question_text: Fix a compact connected Sasaki manifold with a fixed contact CR structure (D, J), and consider its Sasaki cone t^+(D, J), whose points are compatible Reeb vector fields and whose rays are equivalence classes under positive transverse scaling. Must every ray in this Sasaki cone that carries a constant scalar curvature Sasaki metric be isolated among all rays in the cone, or can there exist non-isolated families of constant scalar curvature rays?
accepted.context_brief: Isolation of cscS rays in the Sasaki cone

evidence.quote: This leads to two important open problems: Problem 1. Are constant scalar curvature rays in the Sasaki cone isolated?
So Sasakian structures in t +(D, J) come in rays
An important special case are the Sasaki metrics of constant scalar curvature (cscS)

accepted.question_text: Fix a compact connected Sasaki manifold with a fixed contact CR structure (D, J), and let its Sasaki cone consist of the compatible Reeb vector fields for that structure. Suppose this cone contains extremal Sasaki rays, meaning rays represented by Sasaki metrics that are critical points of the Calabi functional, equivalently metrics whose scalar curvature has transversely holomorphic gradient. Does it then follow that the same Sasaki cone must contain at least one ray carrying a constant scalar curvature Sasaki metric?
accepted.context_brief: Existence of a cscS ray when extremal rays exist

evidence.quote: Problem 2. If there are extremal rays of Sasaki metrics in the Sasaki cone, is there always at least one constant scalar curvature ray?
whose critical points are those Sasaki metrics whose (1, 0) gradient ∂#sg of the scalar curvature sg is transversely holomorphic. Such Sasaki metrics (structures) are called extremal.
So extremal and cscS Sasakian structures come in rays.
